items.notes: From the cycle-9 TASTE pass, finding 1 (notable) -- the headline taste finding of run #3. CONDUCTOR-MEASURED, and the agent's figure was CONSERVATIVE: the corpus is 50 entries, so under uniform draws the MEDIAN first exact repeat lands at draw 9 and P(repeat by draw 12) = 76.2%. The agent reported feeling it at use 12; the arithmetic says most users feel it sooner. Severity 'notable' rather than 'fundamental' was CHECKED, not rubber-stamped: the SHAPE of the product (one quiet attributed line, pipeable, stderr-clean) held across 32 runs and is genuinely good; it is the POOL that runs out. The daily --seed MOTD pattern (7 distinct aphorisms across a simulated week) partially masks the repeat and is the product's strongest idea. || RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY at run #4 cycle 9 by a fresh taste agent that had never seen TS-1, and CORROBORATED — recorded here rather than filed as new backlog (the cycle-6 dedupe rule: an independent instrument re-deriving a known gap is corroboration, not new work). Two things are genuinely NEW. (a) A SECOND FRAME: TS-1 measured within-SESSION repeat (median first repeat at draw 9). The new agent measured the DAILY-MOTD frame the spec actually pitches — P(at least one repeat across 7 daily draws) = 1-(50/50)(49/50)...(44/50) = 35.56%, so roughly a third of users see a rerun in their first week. Conductor recomputed independently: 35.56% vs the agent's 35.6% (gate cell B1, with must-die control C2). (b) A DIFFERENT REMEDY: TS-1 assumes the fix is corpus GROWTH; the new agent points out that a recency guard (never repeat the immediately-previous pick) or a first-class --daily flag would kill the worst case WITHOUT expanding the corpus — a remedy that does not require lifting the corpus-expansion non-goal, though it does require lifting the rotation non-goal. Conductor live-measured 200 default draws: 50/50 distinct, 4 immediate back-to-back repeats against a uniform expectation of 3.98 — so the draw is uniform and the defect is DESIGN (no rotation), not a biased RNG. Gate cells C3/C4/C5/C6/C7. || THIRD INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION, run #5 cycle 9, by a fresh taste agent told not to read the journal, backlog or REPORT.md. Corroborated again; still not filed as new work. The agent felt the first repeat at use 12 (run #4's agent: also 12). CONDUCTOR-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY at gate cells A2/A3/A4 and the draw is WORSE than either agent felt: in a fresh 40-draw sample the first repeat landed at use 3, with 24/40 distinct against a with-replacement expectation of 27.7; a 30-draw sample gave 22/30 against an expectation of 22.7 and reproduced the agent's reported 22/30 EXACTLY. Cell A4 is the must-live control: the same counter reports 40/40 on a deliberately repeat-free sequence, so the repeat counts are a property of the draw and not of the instrument -- a rotation implementation could not have produced any of these numbers. The agent independently reached run #4's recency-guard remedy ("at minimum never repeat the immediately previous draw"), from scratch. Three passes across three runs now agree, which is why this is the standing operator lever and not an open question.

items.title: Seven CLI behaviours are unspecified and a human should rule on them (from J-6 + N-4 + D-44 + Q-7 + TS-5)
items.acceptance: A human rules on SEVEN behaviours the Domain rules do not currently decide (two enumerated inline below; five more — D-42, D-43, D-44, D-45, D-46 — enumerated in the notes and written up in SPEC.md § Undecided behaviours), and the ruling is written into SPEC.md as an explicit clause either way. (1) --help vs usage-error precedence when both appear in argv: the shipped behaviour is that the usage error WINS in both argv orders (measured: `--help --seed abc` and `--seed abc --help` both exit 2 with "aphorism: flag --seed requires a numeric value" on stderr). (2) Whether `--seed -0` and `--seed 0` are THE SAME SEED: they are `===` in JavaScript, but toUint32Seed folds the IEEE-754 bit pattern including the sign bit, so they select DIFFERENT aphorisms (measured: seed 0 -> Kernighan "most effective debugging tool"; seed -0 -> Saint-Exupery "Perfection is achieved"). Either behaviour is defensible; the SPEC decides neither.
items.notes:
FILED AT CYCLE 4 from J-6, which measured both and correctly declined to pin either with a test. This is a SPEC decision, not a swarm task, and it is filed the way T-040 is: a human ratifies or reverses, and the item is not dispatchable until they do.

WHY NO TEST WAS ADDED, and why that was right: the Domain rules resolve exactly ONE flag-vs-error precedence question explicitly — for --list ("A seed that fails to parse is still a usage error under --list"). The existence of that carve-out is evidence the author does not treat "usage-error trumps other flags" as self-evidently general; where they meant it to generalise, they said so. They never said it for --help. An assertion pinning today s behaviour would therefore be a future false rejection rather than coverage — which is the failure mode J-6 exists to avoid. Same logic for -0/0: the rule guarantees determinism PER SEED VALUE and says nothing about whether -0 and 0 are one value or two.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RULES ON (2): if the answer is "they are the same seed", that is a PRODUCT bug in toUint32Seed and closing it is a src/ change, which this run s non-goals fence off. If the answer is "they are distinguishable bit patterns, by design", the fix is one SPEC sentence and nothing else. The cheap ruling and the expensive one are not symmetric, so rule before anyone writes code.

HONEST NOTE ON (1) FROM THE BUILDER, disclosed before any gate looked: its "does not map" call on case 1 rests on an INFERENCE from the --list carve-out (silence implies deliberate scoping) rather than on direct textual statement. A reasonable reviewer could read the Exit-codes clause as unconditional and call the current behaviour a hole rather than an unspecified choice. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. | CYCLE 4: N-4 added TWO more rulings to this item, both measured. (3) REPEATED --tag/--author (D-42): shipped behaviour is last-occurrence-wins and it is UNPROTECTED - conductor reproduced it independently (--tag humor --tag design --list prints the 14-entry design list; a first-wins mutant prints the 9-entry humor list; the suite stays 102p/0f on both). SPEC spells every filter flag in the singular and never mentions repetition, so last-wins is an artifact of assignment order in parseArgs, not a contract. (4) EMPTY/WHITESPACE --seed (D-43): SPEC Selection says --seed accepts any value that Number() parses to a non-NaN number, and Number("")===0 is non-NaN, so the literal reading says ACCEPT; the implementation rejects with exit 2 and SPEC Exit-codes calls a missing flag argument bad usage. The two clauses point opposite ways, so there is no decided behaviour to test against - a human must pick one.

|| STATUS todo -> BLOCKED at cycle 5, as backlog hygiene, NOT as a failure and NOT as a drop. This item needs four CLI behaviours the Domain rules do not decide — --help-vs-usage-error precedence, -0/0 seed identity, repeated --tag/--author, and empty/whitespace --seed. It sat as `todo` on a board that a conductor walks top-down looking for dispatchable work, which is exactly the churn K-5 exists to prevent — N-8's own acceptance forbids re-opening these as agent work. It is now BLOCKED on a named human actor and fully restated in REPORT.md § "Improvement run #3 — human-owned items, hand-off" (appended cycle 5, verified by the conductor). attempts stays 0: nothing was tried and failed, so an attempts bump would misreport the history. Unblocks the moment a human rules; nothing in the swarm can unblock it. CYCLE 6 CORROBORATION + one new fact. The cycle-6 QA live-look, an instrument with no knowledge of D-43, independently re-derived the empty-seed gap from the shipped binary and reached the same two-clauses-point-opposite-ways reading. Independent re-derivation raises confidence that this gap is real and human-owned, and it cost nothing to learn because the agent was not told the answer. NEW FACT for whoever rules, which D-43 does NOT record: the refusal is specific to EMPTY and WHITESPACE-ONLY values. Whitespace-PADDED values are ACCEPTED today — `node bin/aphorism.js --seed " 5 " --json` is byte-identical to `--seed 5` and exits 0 (conductor-measured, cycle 6, .swarm/runs/cycle-006-qa-verify.txt). So the implementation is not uniformly "trim then reject"; src/args.js:55 rejects only when the trimmed value is empty, then hands the UNTRIMMED string to Number(), which itself tolerates padding. A ruling of "accept per Number()" is therefore a smaller change than it looks: it deletes one guard clause rather than reworking seed parsing.

|| CYCLE 13, RUN #3 review-fix pass: a FIFTH ruling joins this item. (5) EMPTY FLAG VALUE, '=' FORM vs SPACE FORM (D-44). Reviewer-found, then independently reproduced by an adversarial verifier, then re-measured by the conductor. Shipped behaviour: --author '' returns exit code 0 and prints an aphorism (--author '' --list piped to wc -l gives 50, identical to --list piped to wc -l, i.e. the whole corpus); --author= returns exit code 2; --tag '' returns exit code 1; --tag= returns exit code 2. Mechanism: src/args.js:83-86 (the equals branch) deliberately rejects an empty value, while the space branch at src/args.js:106-124 checks only for a missing next token or one that looksLikeFlag(), so it assigns the empty string at line 121. The verifier ruled UNDECIDED, not a violation, and the reasoning is recorded in SPEC.md D-44: Exit-codes calls a missing flag argument bad usage and the equals-branch rejection is a deliberate line of code (arguing defect), but a shell passing '' DID supply an argument, and the space-form results follow mechanically from two clauses the SPEC does state — substring containment necessarily matches everything on an empty needle, whole-tag equality necessarily matches nothing. Two stated clauses point opposite ways and none names empty values. NO CODE CHANGE WAS MADE, and independently of the ruling none should be made by the swarm: either direction changes shipped user-visible CLI behaviour, which this run's non-goals forbid.

|| COUNT DEBT CREATED BY THIS EDIT, DECLARED RATHER THAN PAID (cycle 13). Raising this item from four behaviours to five makes REPORT.md § 'J-7: Four CLI behaviours...' (line ~1300) stale by one. It is NOT repaired in this cycle: this cycle's verification gate was sealed before dispatch and does not cover REPORT.md, and an unverified document edit smuggled in at persist time is exactly the discipline this run exists to hold. Filed as R-2, which also picks up three PRE-EXISTING stale mentions this cycle discovered but did not create (REPORT.md lines ~1062, ~1230, ~1244 all still say 'two behaviours', against a backlog title that has said four since cycle 4). Cycle 12 repaired the § heading alone and did not sweep the body — the same decay class, one layer down.

|| RUN #4 CYCLE 8: a SIXTH ruling joins this item, routed here by Q-7. (6) EXIT CODE 3 IS NOT IN THE SPEC EXIT-CODES ENUMERATION (measured gap D-45). Shipped behaviour: bin/aphorism.js exits 3 on a write failure, on BOTH streams — a non-EPIPE stdout failure (one `aphorism: ...` diagnostic on stderr) and a non-EPIPE stderr failure (NO diagnostic anywhere, and the exit code the run had already earned, 1 or 2, is deliberately replaced). The SPEC Domain rule still reads "Exit codes: 0 success, 1 no match, 2 bad usage". CHRONOLOGY, which is why no clause ever covered it: exit 3 landed at run #3 cycle 8, four cycles AFTER the 43-clause coverage map was derived at run #3 cycle 4. The clash a human must settle: if the Exit-codes clause is a CLOSED enumeration, shipped exit 3 violates the regression floor; if it is OPEN, exit 3 is an unlisted-but-legal addition and the clause needs a sentence saying so. This run may not amend a Domain rule — the Domain-rules header calls those clauses the regression floor and the 29-clause coverage map is measured against them — so the gap is RECORDED in SPEC.md § Undecided behaviours and routed here, never repaired. The TEST suite does cover exit 3 (test/pipe.test.js:86 and :160, both exercising /dev/full, 0 skipped in the 118/118 run), so this is a SPEC and README gap, not a test hole.

|| RUN #4 CYCLE 11: a SEVENTH ruling joins this item, routed here by TS-5. (7) THE TASTE NOTE PROMISES A DIM ATTRIBUTION AND NOTHING STYLES IT (measured gap D-46). SPEC § Taste notes asserts "Attribution is dim, not loud; the aphorism is the product". Shipped: bin/aphorism.js:60 formats every result as `${entry.text}\n    — ${entry.author}` and there is no ANSI escape and no isTTY branch anywhere in bin/aphorism.js, src/args.js or src/select.js (conductor-scanned, 3/3 false); `--seed 7 | od -c` carries zero ESC bytes. So the attribution is byte-identical in weight to the aphorism, distinguished only by a four-space indent and an em dash. The clash a human must settle: either the taste note overstates what ships, or the product under-delivers its own aesthetic. The SPEC contains both the claim AND, in Nice-to-haves (SPEC.md:160, "ANSI dim for the attribution line, respecting NO_COLOR"), the tacit admission that it is not built — which is evidence for the second reading but not proof, since a Nice-to-have is not a statement about what already ships. NO CODE CHANGE, and none should be made by the swarm: NO_COLOR is a locked non-goal of this run (SPEC.md:314). || COUNT DEBT PAID IN THE SAME CYCLE, not declared and deferred as at cycle 13 of run #3: this item's title moved six -> seven, its acceptance clause moved FIVE -> SEVEN (it had been stale by one since D-45 landed at cycle 8 — found while raising the count, not reported by anyone), and REPORT.md's J-7 bullet moved six -> seven with the seventh behaviour written into its enumeration. docs/report-history.md was deliberately NOT touched: it carries eleven stale J-7 figures and that is CORRECT, because it is the archive of what past reports said, moved there under this run's own M-2. Rewriting it would falsify the record of what was believed when. A gate cell pins it byte-identical.

The forensic history that made the file 1578 lines is still present in full - MOVED verbatim into a linked appendix, not summarized, not paraphrased, not dropped - and every cross-reference between the two documents resolves to something that exists.
items.notes: HIGHEST-RISK ITEM OF THE RUN. M-2's own rule is mechanical: every non-whitespace line of today's REPORT.md must still appear in the concatenation of the new REPORT.md and the appendix. Move sections BYTE-FOR-BYTE; write only the new first-screen summary fresh. items.title: The README self-guard that caught this cycle's stale citation is not mechanized anywhere that survives the run
items.acceptance: README §Node support names its own falsifier as an executable command and that is the ONLY reason cycle 3 could catch the citation going stale — but nothing was running it, and the cell that now does (G12) lives in SWARM/runs and dies with this run. A test in test/ runs the section's own quoted `git diff <base>..HEAD -- <paths>` command, parsed out of the prose rather than hardcoded, and fails when it returns non-empty. It MUST DEGRADE, NOT FAIL, on a shallow clone: CI checks out with --depth=1, so when the base commit is unreachable (`git cat-file -e <base>^{commit}` non-zero) the test skips with a stated reason rather than turning the matrix red for the wrong cause. Prove both arms: the test must fail against a deliberately stale base, pass against the current one, and skip (not fail) in a shallow clone.
items.notes: Filed by cycle 3 out of its own finding. The general shape is the valuable part: a doc claim that names the command which falsifies it is checkable forever; one that does not is only ever checkable by a human who happens to wonder. Scoped as test hardening (explicitly in this run's brief), not a feature: no new flag, no user-visible behaviour, and it raises the suite count, which the P-5 floor (>=119) permits. CLOSED cycle 5, 9/9 sealed gate (sha256 8e658830, byte-unchanged after scoring), both pure-assertion cells control-proven failable. Delivered as test/node-support-citation.test.js, byte-identical to what the builder returned — the README re-citation in c0337f1 is a CONSEQUENCE of the item, not a repair of the deliverable. The gate caught, before anything was committed, that the new test lives inside the pathspec README cites, so the guard falsifies the citation it guards the instant it lands; resolved by the CI round trip the section itself prescribes (run 32328776838 at 5f833ab, four jobs green, 1 skipped on every one). items.title: P-5 (green at every commit) and P-6 (the self-falsifying citation guard) are in direct conflict, and only a human can rule on which gives
items.acceptance: A human rules on ONE of: (a) P-5 wording is amended to exempt the single commit that introduces a src/bin/test/.github change from the full-clone green requirement, on the stated ground that the CI run which refreshes the citation cannot exist before the push; (b) the citation design changes so the window closes; or (c) the guard is retired. Until then the exception stands recorded, never re-labelled as a pass.
items.notes: MEASURED cycle 5, not inferred. P-6 mechanizes README Node-support own falsifier. Because the pathspec it cites is `src bin test .github`, ANY commit touching those paths makes the cited diff non-empty at that commit, so the suite is RED on a full clone until a follow-up commit re-cites to a CI run for it — and that CI run cannot exist until after the push. Commit 5f833ab is exactly that case: red on a full clone, green in CI (the guard skips on depth-1 checkout), repaired by c0337f1. P-5 requires green at >=119 on EVERY commit this run makes, so 5f833ab is a genuine exception and is recorded as one in .swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-P-6.txt. WHY THIS IS HUMAN-OWNED: every available disposition edits a locked SPEC must-have or deletes a shipped claim, and this run non-goals forbid the swarm doing either for itself. Note the window is not a defect in the test — it is the price of the claim being checkable at all, and the alternative (a citation nothing runs) is the state that let the claim go stale undetected two cycles ago.

items.title: The citation guard cannot fire on the commit that breaks it, so main is red for a whole cycle
items.value: restores "green at every commit" (P-5) to something a pre-commit run can actually check
items.acceptance: The Node-support citation guard evaluates its cited diff against the WORKING TREE, not only against committed history, so a falsification still sitting unstaged is visible to the pre-commit suite run. Concretely: the guard today runs the README's cited `git diff <base>..HEAD -- <paths>`, and HEAD by definition excludes uncommitted work, so the commit that breaks the citation always tests green and the NEXT full-clone run pays for it. Adding the base-to-worktree comparison (the same pathspec, no ..HEAD) closes that. Both arms must be proven: a must-die control where an uncommitted edit to a pathspec file is caught pre-commit, and a must-live control where an uncommitted edit OUTSIDE the pathspec (e.g. README.md itself) does not trip it. The existing skip-on-shallow behaviour must be unchanged -- verify CI still reports the guard as skipped, not failed.
items.notes: Filed run #5 cycle 9, from the red main this cycle repaired. NOT a new discovery of the MECHANISM -- README §Node support limit 2 (cycle 5) already records the transient-red window as intrinsic and knowingly accepted, and this cycle initially mis-framed it as a new instrument defect before reading that note. What IS new is the consequence nobody wrote down: "transient" only holds if the SAME commit repairs the citation, and nothing enforces that. Cycles 5 and 6 repaired in-commit by hand; cycle 8 bumped the CI actions and did not, so c9dd7ff sat red on a full clone for an entire cycle. Measured, not inferred: `git diff c08562b..057d00c -- src bin test .github` (cycle 8's PRE-commit HEAD) is EMPTY, which is why cycle 8's suite run reported 120/120/0 green, while the same diff against c9dd7ff carries the 2-line action bump. CI could not catch it either: it checks out shallow and the guard skips (the "1 skipped" in all four rows of run 32335038575). So no signal available to the breaking commit can observe the break. This item removes the hand-discipline dependency rather than relying on the next conductor remembering.
